subject: ISV connector: intermittent 429s on bulk sync — rapid response plan
messages:
From: Support Team <integrations@harbriclabs.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk sync 429s (affecting several customers)

Hi Olga,

We're seeing intermittent 429s from Redwood during our nightly bulk import window (started ~00:30 PT). We've attached a trimmed log dump (harbric_logs_0624.txt) showing repeated token-throttling responses tied to /v1/generate endpoints. This is impacting three of our mutual customers; ingestion backpressure is causing retries and duplicates.

Can you confirm if you rolled any routing or rate-limiting changes overnight? We need a short-term mitigation (rate bump, retry-backoff guidance) and a timeline for a root-cause fix.

- Sofia Ramos
Integrations Lead, Harbric Labs
sofia.r@harbriclabs.com

Attachments: harbric_logs_0624.txt
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Support Team <integrations@harbriclabs.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk sync 429s (affecting several customers)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the heads up and the logs. Sorry for the disruption.

Quick answers up front:
- We did a minor routing adjustment to improve latency for bursty tenants at 00:15 PT; that could explain the behavior you saw.
- Short-term mitigation: we'll temporarily lift the per-account concurrency cap for your partner tenant and add a tuned retry policy on our side for 12 hours.

Plan:
1) Ben (Support) will validate the logs and confirm the effective throttle signature.
2) I will open an incident and flip the temporary cap (expected within 30 minutes).
3) We'll schedule a joint war-room if the elevated cap doesn't resolve the backlog by EOD.

I'll follow up with actions and a link to the incident bridge.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Partner Success, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, integrations@harbriclabs.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk sync 429s (affecting several customers)

Olga / Sofia — I dug into the truncated logs and correlation ids. The 429 payloads match our token-exhaustion guard where concurrent requests from the same api-key exceed the concurrency profile. The routing change altered how requests were hashed across backends which increased hot-shard pressure for a subset of keys.

Immediate steps I'm taking now (in progress):
- Flipping partner concurrency cap for harbric-prod key + add a temporary token-bucket buffer (will log events instead of dropping) — ETA 20 minutes.
- Pushing a patch to backoff logic to prefer exponential jitter for 429 -> ETA 3 hours to roll to staging.
- Collecting full trace spans and will share a Drive link.

Request for Harbric: please share one full failing request-id from the attached file so I can trace spans across services.

Ben Carter
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.r@harbriclabs.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk sync 429s (affecting several customers)

Thanks Ben, attaching a sample failing request id: req_7f8b2e (see note in harbric_logs_0624.txt). We reproduced the 429 consistently on our side when running parallel imports at 8c/worker.

We've also opened an internal ticket to throttle our client-side concurrency if you think that's the right short-term path. If you can provide the jitter/backoff window recommendation, we'll implement that immediately.

Sofia Ramos
Integrations Lead, Harbric Labs

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, integrations@harbriclabs.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk sync 429s (affecting several customers)

Thanks everyone for the quick turn here. Summary and commitments:

- Temporary mitigation applied: partner concurrency cap lifted and token-bucket buffer enabled (applied 2027-06-24 10:45 PT). Backlog cleared for the three reported customers; we've validated ingestion without duplicates.
- Short-term change: Ben will ship the jittered exponential backoff to staging by 15:30 PT today and begin a progressive rollout.
- Customer ask: Harbric to implement client-side cap at 6 concurrent workers with exponential jitter (base 300ms, max 5s) — Harbric agreed to roll this tonight.
- Post-incident work: owners — Redwood infra (Ben) to produce a postmortem; Partnerships (Olga) to update the partner runbook with escalation steps and per-tenant cap guidance. Marissa will coordinate a joint review with Harbric next week.

I've attached the runbook stub we've started (redwood_runbook_v1.pdf) — please add comments in the Drive link. If anyone wants a standing weekly sync for the integration, propose a cadence and I'll set the invite.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_runbook_v1.pdf
